record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.context_brief: Non-normal trapped ray families in R3
record.original_question: In three-dimensional space, can one trap a two-parameter family of rays that is not normal to any hypersurface, that is, a non-normal 2-parameter family of rays?

evidence.quote: Question 2: In R^3, can one trap a non-normal 2-parameter family of rays?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in three-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$. A "ray" is an oriented straight line (or a directed line segment that may be reflected by mirrors). The space of oriented lines in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is four-dimensional, and a smooth two-parameter family of rays is a smooth two-dimensional submanifold of this space. Such a family is called normal if there exists a smooth hypersurface (a surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$) to which every ray of the family is orthogonal; otherwise the family is called non-normal.

Given a (possibly disconnected) domain $D \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ whose boundary consists of perfectly reflecting mirrors together with a (possibly small) aperture, we say that a two-parameter family of rays is trapped by $D$ if every ray of the family enters $D$ through the aperture and, after undergoing the (specular) reflections off $\partial D$, never exits $D$.

Question: Does there exist a domain $D \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ with reflecting boundary (and an aperture) that traps some non-normal two-parameter family of rays? Equivalently, can one design a mirror configuration in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that traps a 2-parameter family of rays which is not orthogonal to any hypersurface?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a 2021/2022 collection of open problems on billiards and geometric optics, listed as an unsolved question. No subsequent work resolving the trapping of non-normal 2-parameter families of rays in $\mathbb{R}^3$ was located in the search; related results concern normal families and 1-parameter trapping via confocal parabolas. Status appears to remain open.
